findings: The claimed Java paint-state account is locally correct. USymbolStack applies HColors.none() without clearing stroke width, and SvgGraphics.styleMe serializes stroke-width whenever the active width is nonzero.

The Rust production diff is correspondingly narrow and honest: it threads the existing stroke_width argument into the transparent inset rect style and introduces no new parity constants or fixture-shaped production logic.
The preserved held-out checker_explicit_scale_folder_stack_file now passes /private/tmp/rustuml-integrate-20260731a/target/release/examples/diff_one --no-oracle.

However, the first fresh valid counterexample already rejects the change. With roundcorner zero on an empty stack leaf, Java removes rounded geometry entirely, while Rust still emits rx/ry and rounded arc segments. That is executable product drift on a fresh axis and is sufficient for rejection under the T14 rules.

The second fresh valid counterexample rejects even though the target mechanism itself appears fixed: the transparent rect style contains stroke-width:1.625 in both outputs, but the stack cluster envelope, title baseline, child boxes, and root height are all shifted upward on the Rust side by the scaled stroke amount.

The third fresh valid counterexample rejects for two broader reasons: Rust still hardcodes the stack corner radius from its local package constant instead of using the configured roundcorner value that Java passes through USymbolStack, and it repeats the stack-cluster vertical-origin drift under dpi scaling.

Because all three fresh perturbations are valid Java inputs, have preserved Java SVGs, and fail through the shipped no-oracle comparator, the checker verdict must be REJECT even though the narrow transparent-stroke-state insight itself is real.
verdict_reason: I found three valid fresh no-oracle counterexamples at the requested Rust and Java revisions. The preserved stack/folder/file input now passes, but the broader stack symbol model still diverges on zero-roundcorner geometry, configured roundcorner propagation, and stack-cluster vertical placement, so this mechanism cannot be accepted yet.
